current.text: He is 36 years old and is coming back from a torn Achilles.
Portland reportedly plans to start him next to Ja Morant. The projected starting five is Lillard, Morant, Camara, Avdija and Clingan.
He is expected to play about 30 to 31 minutes as a low-minute starter. One expert rejects the view that he is washed or will only play about 25 minutes.
Portland's backcourt is crowded with on-ball guards. Ja Morant, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson and Deni Avdija all share the ball with him.
Experts see the crowded guard group as a risk to his usage. They expect minutes and usage to swing from game to game, and they doubt a trade will consolidate the guards.
Portland's poor finishers (Camara, Clingan, Avdija) are expected to cut how many of the guards' passes turn into assists.
The experts disagree on back-to-backs. One preview does not expect Portland to hold him out of them. Another note flags worry about back-to-backs early in the season.
Portland has three back-to-backs during the fantasy playoff weeks.
The newer expert calls say he will beat his draft price on a per-game basis. One expert drafted him in round 7 and thinks he could be a top 50 player per game. Games played is the main risk.

durable.text: He tore his Achilles. The experts flag injury risk from his age, the Achilles and possible compensation injuries.
He is a very good shooter when playing off the ball.
His FT% is elite and comes on real volume, so he clearly lifts a team's FT%.
His FG% is weak for a guard, so he suits a punt FG% build.

note: He ranks 67th on Yahoo and 70th on ESPN, with an average cost near 5 USD on both sites. Yahoo values him at 16 USD, so in a 144-player auction he could be a cheap source of FT%, threes and assists, and he fits best in punt FG% builds. Early in the season, check his minutes next to Morant and Holiday and whether he plays back-to-backs, since three playoff back-to-backs and his Achilles make games played the main risk.
